title: On Premise Workflow Automation License Cost in 2026
summary: On-premise workflow automation license cost is just one part of your total investment.
body_markdown:
## Self-hosted tools with a published license price


Of the tools here, only n8n and[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/makecom-self-hosted-options-and-alternatives-2026) let you run the workflow engine on your own servers. In each case the published price covers only part of what you'll pay.


Read the pricing page for what the vendor will state; the quote tells you the rest. Each block below names its source, and you should record the date you read it.


### n8n self-hosted pricing


Before you assume your use case is covered, read the license text itself, because the terms limit what you may do commercially. n8n publishes a self-hosted route under its own source-available license, not an OSI-style open-source one.


On strength, n8n offers a mature, widely documented engine. Its limit is that the vendor describes the controls auditors ask about, such as single sign-on and role separation, as paid features. Ask in writing whether it prices them openly or by quote.


Best for teams with an engineer who will own upgrades, backups and the database. Source: n8n's pricing and license pages.


### Activepieces self-hosted editions


Alongside its cloud service, Activepieces has a self-hosted edition. The vendor's pricing page ladders from a free tier, through self-serve paid tiers limited by active flows, up to an Enterprise tier sold by contacting sales.


The page also lists SSO, audit logs and custom roles against tiers. Read it as a map of where the quote begins: the controls a compliance reviewer asks about sit toward the top of that ladder, not at the bottom.


Most vendors keep the full control set for their cloud and **ship a thinner self-hosted build, but Activepieces doesn't** : the list a compliance reviewer asks for (SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, release management, secret managers) is the same in the air-gapped edition as in the managed cloud.


Regulated and public-sector organisations run that air-gapped edition in production, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces as well. The pricing page doesn't say which tier covers a self-hosted install, so get that in writing.


Where n8n's permissive-versus-source-available line matters to you, Activepieces has an MIT-licensed core, 750 integrations counted from its open source monorepo, and roughly 60% of them contributed by the community, so you aren't locked into a vendor's development roadmap.


Best for teams that can run it themselves and will accept a sales conversation for the audit-grade features. Source: Activepieces' pricing page.


### Microsoft Power Automate on-premises


You don't get a self-hosted engine with Power Automate. Flows run in Microsoft's cloud, and the on-premises integration is a gateway that lets those cloud flows reach data inside your network.


Even desktop automation, which runs on your machines, is still licensed and managed by Microsoft through the cloud service. So your automation stops when Microsoft's cloud does, even if your database stays up.


Best for organizations already licensed for Microsoft 365 whose requirement is reaching on-premises data, not hosting the engine. Source: Microsoft's Power Automate pricing and documentation pages.
